units.sentence: 2027 funding for the jail, courts, prosecutors and public defender's office isn't known as of Nov 8, 2026.
units.marker: {analysis: the budget page on Nov 8 had no 2027 proposal (P-045)}
units.reason: P-045 (captured Nov 8, 2026) lists only FY2026 documents, so no 2027 proposal was posted. With no proposal and no adoption, 2027 funding for these offices isn't known. The offices named match the six leaders (sheriff/jail, prosecutors, courts, public defender; P-069).

units.sentence: The public defender's office defends people charged with crimes who can't afford a lawyer.
units.reason: No passage defines the office, so the {analysis} tag is right. The definition is accurate in plain language: a public defender's office represents people charged with crimes who can't afford a lawyer.

units.sentence: The solicitor-general's office prosecutes less serious crimes, called misdemeanors.
units.marker: {analysis: plain-language definition; P-062 cites ABA benchmarks for misdemeanor prosecution among the office's challenges}
units.reason: Accurate plain-language definition (Georgia's solicitors-general prosecute misdemeanors in state court). The tag describes P-062 correctly: its CHALLENGES list includes "Compliance with ABA processing benchmarks for misdemeanor prosecution." P-062 is consistent with the definition but doesn't establish it alone, so tagging rather than citing is right.

units.sentence: A FOX 5 report says a directive asked departments to limit 2027 requests for extra money to "5% above current allocations."
units.evidence_span: a directive asking all county departments to limit any request for additional funding to 5% above current allocations
units.reason: P-077 (FOX 5, S21; P-080 names FOX 5 Atlanta) describes the directive in these terms, "for the upcoming 2027 ... budget". The quote is verbatim. Like FOX 5, the sentence names no issuer.

units.sentence: Commissioner Barrett's resolution says the commission restricted requests to 5% of each department's "base budget."
units.evidence_span: the newly established Budget Commission has restricted all departments to making budget requests that do not exceed 5% of their “base budget” for 2027
units.reason: P-029 (Resolution 26-0729's text, S04d) says this; P-032 shows Barrett sponsored it; "base budget" is verbatim. The claim is attributed to the resolution, not to Barrett personally. A clarity point about "requests" is under framing_issues.

units.sentence: The Board set the resolution aside (filed it) on Nov 4.
units.marker: {analysis: status "Filed" after a Nov 4 vote to file, with no later step (P-024, P-025)}
units.reason: P-024's status is "Filed". P-025's last action (2026-11-04) is a substitute motion "to file" that passed, and P-025 is the whole history, so there is no later step. "Set aside" is a fair plain-language gloss of filing, correctly tagged as analysis.

units.sentence: Option C, a proposal to change how drafts are built, was set aside (filed) on Nov 4.
units.marker: {analysis: status "Filed" after a Nov 4 vote to file, with no later step (P-024, P-025)}
units.reason: Same basis as L121 (P-024 status "Filed"; P-025 Nov 4 motion to file passed; no later step). "A proposal to change how drafts are built" describes Resolution 26-0729 (P-024, P-030) fairly but vaguely (see framing_issues).

units.sentence: Resolution 26-0460, which Commissioner Bob Ellis and Vice Chair Khadijah Abdur-Rahman sponsored, says today's Budget Commission adds "earlier and ongoing input," with north-south "balanced representation."
units.evidence_span: with earlier and ongoing input from members of the Board, structured to ensure balanced representation from both the northern and southern portions of Fulton County
units.reason: Both quotes are verbatim in P-004. "Adds" paraphrases "combines ... with", and the line's lead-in ("Board input") supplies the truncated "from members of the Board". P-016 lists Ellis as sponsor and Abdur-Rahman as co-sponsor, and P-017's "(Ellis/Abdur-Rahman)" supports naming both. The words are the resolution's, not a statement by either sponsor.

units.sentence: Chief Probate Judge Kenya Johnson, for six justice officials, said they decline to join "a process that unnecessarily limits the voices of the justice system."
units.evidence_span: We respectfully decline to participate in a process that unnecessarily limits the voices of the justice system
units.reason: The quote is verbatim in P-078. P-078 says Johnson spoke "on behalf of the coalition", and P-076 names its six members. "Decline to join" paraphrases "respectfully decline to participate in". Missing date and context are under framing_issues.

units.sentence: Resolution 26-0729 (Option C), which Commissioner Dana Barrett sponsored, says listing requests in the proposed budget has let the Board "get a true picture of the departments’ needs."
units.evidence_span: Fulton County has traditionally included departmental budget “enhancement requests” in its publicly available Proposed Budget, which has allowed the Board of Commissioners to get a true picture of the departments’ needs
units.problem: Minor: P-028 is about including "enhancement requests" (requests for extra money), so "listing requests" is a little broader than the source. Card 3 (L203) renders the same clause more exactly as "departments' extra requests".
units.suggested_fix: ...says listing extra requests in the proposed budget has let the Board "get a true picture of the departments’ needs."
units.reason: The quote is verbatim in P-028, curly apostrophe included. P-032 and P-024's "(Barrett)" give the sponsor, and P-024's title supplies "informed decision-making".

units.sentence: Two sides claim transparency: Option C aims "to ensure transparency," and Commissioner Ellis said today's process is "more transparent and open" than in recent years.
units.marker: {analysis: Option C's title is in P-024 and P-027; Ellis's statement is P-073, a comparison card 4 rates Uncertain}
units.reason: "to ensure transparency" is verbatim in P-024's title (P-027 has it in capitals). "more transparent and open" is verbatim in P-073 ("than anything we’ve had in recent years"), and card 4's label rates that comparison Uncertain. Calling these two of the guide's three groups "two sides" is a fair synthesis.

units.sentence: Each side gets one line, so the justice officials' requests for more money and a January vote are on cards 6 and 5.
units.marker: {editorial: one line per side; the officials' line is their primary objection (P-076)}
units.problem: "Side" is not defined here and conflicts with the page's own usage. The cards' Side field puts the officials (card 2) and Resolution 26-0729 (card 3) on the same side, "critical of the current process", and L8 groups Barrett with the officials as objectors. By position, the guide gives the critical side two lines (L133, L134) and the supporting side one (L132), plus a shared note (L135). The sentence therefore claims a balance the guide doesn't have.
units.suggested_fix: Say "Each group gets one line" (or name the three groups). Or say that two of the three lines come from critics because the sources quote more critics (as L164 says).
units.reason: The card mapping is right: more money is card 6 and the January vote is card 5, and both asks are in P-070. L133 also carries the officials' primary objection (P-076). But "each side gets one line" is true only if "side" means each source group (26-0460's sponsors, the justice officials, Option C's sponsor).

units.sentence: The 2026 plan leaves savings about $2.8 million above the least the county must keep.
units.marker: {computed: $179,000,901 − $176,218,666 = $2,782,235, from P-054's "Fund Balance Minimum Reserve" row}
units.reason: Redone: 179,000,901 − 176,218,666 = 2,782,235, about $2.8 million. Both figures are P-054's 2026 Adopted column ("Fund Balance - Ending" $179,000,901; "Fund Balance Minimum Reserve ... Requirement" $176,218,666), and the quoted row name "Fund Balance Minimum Reserve" appears unbroken in P-054. "The least the county must keep" is a fair plain reading of "Minimum Reserve Requirement".

units.reason: P-077 (FOX 5) says this, and the quote is verbatim. "Holds" paraphrases "a directive asking ... to limit". "That limit" points back to "the 5% limit" in the previous sentence.

units.evidence_span: restricted all departments to making budget requests that do not exceed 5% of their “base budget” for 2027

units.sentence: No 2027 source we archived argued against more money for the six offices.
units.marker: {analysis: none of the archived statements does}
units.reason: None of the archived 2027 material argues against more money: Ellis (P-073, P-079), Resolution 26-0460 (P-004), Barrett (P-072) and the officials. The 5% limit is described (P-029, P-077), but no reason or argument for it is archived. The 2026 budget message's "no additional resources available" (P-049) is about 2026, and the sentence's "2027" correctly leaves it out.

units.sentence: The resolutions quoted below are Board records: Resolution 26-0460 (Ellis, Abdur-Rahman; adopted Aug 5, 2026) and Resolution 26-0729 (Barrett; its motion to approve failed Oct 21, and it was filed Nov 4).
units.reason: P-016 and P-017 give the sponsors and "Passed" on 2026-08-05. P-024 has "(MOTION TO APPROVE FAILED ON 10/21/26) (FILED)", status "Filed" and a MatterPassedDate of 2026-11-04. P-032 names Barrett as sponsor.

units.sentence: Filing set Resolution 26-0729 aside without approving it.
units.marker: {analysis: status "Filed" after a Nov 4 vote to file, with no later step (P-024, P-025)}
units.reason: Status "Filed" (P-024). The Oct 21 approval motion failed, no vote was taken on Nov 4's approval motion, and the substitute motion to file passed (P-025), so the resolution was never approved. The "set aside" gloss is correctly tagged.

units.sentence: Resolution 26-0729 says the 5% limit effectively makes the code's rule on requests "impossible."
units.evidence_span: by placing the 5% cap on departmental enhancement requests, the Budget Commission is effectively making its mandate to submit a proposed budget that includes the budget requests of the County’s departments impossible
units.reason: P-029 says this. The "mandate" is Section 2-261's rule, cited in the WHEREAS clause just before. The one-word quote is verbatim and keeps its sense, and the claim is attributed to the resolution.

units.sentence: The code's rule and 2026 practice are on record; the conflict isn't settled.
units.marker: {analysis: the label above names each part; the rule is P-005, and the 2026 draft listed extra requests (P-049, P-046)}
units.reason: P-005 is the code's rule. P-049 ("The enhancement submissions are included as an appendix"), with P-046, shows the 2026 proposal listed extra requests. The card label rates "Conflict with the code" Uncertain. Wording points are under framing_issues.

units.sentence: If the claim is right, all commissioners and staff can hear departments' requests.
units.marker: {analysis: what the card's claim would mean}
units.problem: Minor: Ellis said "their staff" (commissioners' staff). "All commissioners and staff" can be read as all county staff, which is a slightly broader claim than his.
units.suggested_fix: If the claim is right, all commissioners and their staff can hear departments' requests.
units.reason: This follows Ellis's own account of openness in P-073: "all commissioners and their staff are able to attend and hear what is said".

units.sentence: Commissioner Ellis called the commission's meetings "open meetings" and the process "more transparent and open" than in recent years.
units.evidence_span: We have a budget commission. Those meetings are open meetings.
units.reason: Both quotes are verbatim in P-073. "Than anything we’ve had in recent years" is fairly shortened.

units.sentence: Records back the announced hearings, not the comparison.
units.marker: {analysis: P-042 and P-055 to P-058; the comparison is Ellis's, in P-073}
units.reason: P-042 is the county's notice of the six October hearings, and P-055 to P-058 show posted slides. Nothing archived checks Ellis's comparison with past years, and card 4's label rates it Uncertain.

units.sentence: Funding decisions could affect court delays, jail conditions and public safety, justice officials said, Atlanta News First reported.
units.evidence_span: Fulton County justice officials are pushing back against proposed changes to next year’s budget process, warning that funding decisions could affect court delays, jail conditions and public safety
units.reason: P-069 (Atlanta News First, S20) says this. The neutral "said" stands in for "warning".

units.sentence: The officials asked for more money.
units.evidence_span: The officials are also calling for more funding to address what they describe as staffing shortages, court delays and jail overcrowding
units.reason: P-070: "calling for more funding".

units.sentence: County records back added jail-agreement costs, not most other needs.
units.marker: {analysis: P-048 to P-050 and P-054 back the jail-agreement costs; most other needs rest on the offices' slides, P-061 to P-066}
units.problem: Minor (2027 resting on 2026): the card is about 2027 needs, but every county record behind this sentence is from the 2026 cycle (the 2026 adopted budget, and the message sent with the 2026 proposal). There is no 2027 county record yet. With no year in the sentence, a reader may take it as county backing for 2027 jail-agreement costs.
units.suggested_fix: 2026 county records back rising jail-agreement costs, not most other needs.
units.reason: P-054 shows the 2026 "Consent Decree" line raised from $31,843,000 proposed to $50,000,000 adopted. P-049 and P-050 say more resources will be needed and that costs are "expected to grow". Most other needs rest on the offices' own slides; the 2026 solicitor-general increase (P-054) is the main county-record exception, so "most" is right.

units.sentence: When the 2026 proposal was written, consent decree costs were "still being vetted and have not been determined," though the county expected them to grow.
units.evidence_span: To date, all decree compliance related costs are still being vetted and have not been determined, but as costs accelerate from partial year to full year recurring implementation, this number is expected to grow
units.reason: The quote is verbatim in P-050. P-046 says the book reprints the budget message submitted with the FY2026 Proposed Budget, and P-050's "To date" places the statement at that time. "Expected them to grow" matches "this number is expected to grow".

units.sentence: That leaves savings about $2.8 million above the least the county must keep.
units.marker: {computed: $179,000,901 − $176,218,666 = $2,782,235, from P-054's "Fund Balance Minimum Reserve" row}
units.reason: Redone: 179,000,901 − 176,218,666 = 2,782,235, about $2.8 million. Both figures are P-054's 2026 Adopted column ("Fund Balance - Ending" $179,000,901; "Fund Balance Minimum Reserve ... Requirement" $176,218,666), and the quoted row name "Fund Balance Minimum Reserve" appears unbroken in P-054. "The least the county must keep" is a fair plain reading of "Minimum Reserve Requirement". "That" clearly refers to the 2026 plan's use of savings in the previous sentence.

units.sentence: Speak at the Fulton County commissioners' public comment, in person or by Zoom, before the Board adopts the budget.
units.evidence_span: Residents have two options to participate in public comment: in person and virtually via Zoom.
units.reason: P-039 lists the Nov 18, 2026 meeting at 10 a.m. P-036 provides public comment at both regular meetings. P-067 gives in person and Zoom. P-005 sets adoption no later than the second regular meeting in January, and P-014 gives adoption to the full Board. That Nov 18 comes before adoption is an inference, but a safe one: no earlier vote or hearing was noticed by Nov 8 (P-042).

units.sentence: Fulton's Board of Commissioners voted to set aside (file) a resolution to end a limit holding departments' requests to 5% above current funding.
units.marker: {analysis: status "Filed" after a Nov 4 vote to file, with no later step (P-024, P-025); the limit's terms are FOX 5's (P-077)}
units.reason: P-025: the substitute motion to file passed on 2026-11-04 (P-034: 4 yes, 1 no, 1 did not vote). P-024: status "Filed", and the title says "to remove the 5% cap". "5% above current funding" matches FOX 5's "5% above current allocations" (P-077) and agrees in substance with P-029's 5% of "base budget". Attribution is under framing_issues.

framing_issues.text: Each side gets one line, so the justice officials' requests for more money and a January vote are on cards 6 and 5.
framing_issues.issue: Undefined "side", and implied balance. L135 now says "Two sides" (two of three groups), but the cards' Side field and L8 put the officials and Option C on one side, critical of the current process. By position, the values guide gives critics two dedicated lines (L133, L134) and supporters one (L132), plus the shared transparency note. Saying "each side gets one line" hides that 2-to-1 split.

framing_issues.text: Commissioner Barrett's resolution says the commission restricted requests to 5% of each department's "base budget."
framing_issues.issue: The sentence says "requests" without "for extra money", right after FOX 5's "requests for extra money ... 5% above current allocations". Read literally, "5% of" the base budget sounds like a cap on total requests, and the two descriptions seem to contradict each other ("above" vs "of"). P-029 means enhancement requests ("the 5% cap on departmental enhancement requests"). L143 and L166 avoid this because "it" points back to the limit on requests for extra money. Fix: "restricted requests for extra money to 5% of each department's "base budget.""

framing_issues.text: Option C, a proposal to change how drafts are built, was set aside (filed) on Nov 4.
framing_issues.issue: Vague description: the reader isn't told what Option C would change. It would remove the 5% limit and list every request in the draft (L154). Fix: "Option C, a proposal to remove the 5% limit and list every request,".

framing_issues.text: said they decline to join "a process that unnecessarily limits the voices of the justice system."
framing_issues.issue: No date or context. In the present tense, "decline to join" a process can read as a full boycott of budgeting. Per FOX 5, on Oct 7 the officials declined the in-person hearings but still sent written 2027 requests (P-076, P-080). Fix: add "on Oct 7", or "declined to present in person, citing ...".

framing_issues.text: The code's rule and 2026 practice are on record; the conflict isn't settled.
framing_issues.issue: "The conflict isn't settled" assumes a conflict exists, but the label says only that whether there is one is Uncertain. "2026 practice" is undefined within the In short. Fix: "The code's rule and the 2026 draft's list of extra requests are on record; whether the limit conflicts with the rule isn't settled."

framing_issues.text: a resolution to end a limit holding departments' requests to 5% above current funding
framing_issues.issue: The reader-facing text states the limit's terms as fact, with no attribution. The workspace says the exact wording isn't known (L120) and now credits the two descriptions to FOX 5 and to the resolution (L92, L143, L166). The descriptions agree in substance, so the risk is low. Fix: "a resolution to end a 5% limit on departments' requests for extra money".
